chapter: Duke, Eddie Lang and other guitarists
title: Al Casey and knowing the ropes
summary: He did not think much of Al Casey, who knew chords but not enough.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Yeah. What about some of the other players back in the '30s? Do you remember -- did you ever hear Al Casey? You must have heard him.
Yeah. Al Casey. He was colored, wasn't he?
Yeah. I didn't think too much of him, as far as that's concerned, because he was (inaudible). Heard of him.
Yeah. But the ropes, that's what I call them.
Yeah. That's what they call chords, ropes.
Uh-huh. You mean like a boxer?
No. Ropes, you know. He knew the ropes.
Oh, yeah, right. Right. Right. But then you've got to -- you're saying that you have to go beyond that?
Yeah. You had to get knowledge.
